cases.note: zenoh-modem's RF router (Appendix B, `examples/zk2/zenoh-modem/faces/`) over modem.v3, which lists link.v1: what it exposes is its nine frame resources, all packed, so none draws `not_packed` (§2.17); the face lists eight at 60 s, each crossing whole with no downsampling, and denies `frames/message` by name (`frame_unlisted`, §2.7); `frames/link`'s horizon is liveness evidence; one frame a minute replaces each keep-alive, so no `keep_alive_not_suppressed` (§2.16); the catalog the ground holds lists every crossing revision (§2.18)
cases.policy:
# zenoh-modem's RF node (link.v2 Appendix B)
profile  = "link.v2"
system   = "h-3fa9c2d41b7e"
services = ["rf0"]
binding  = "zm-1.10.2-r1"           # the zenoh fork zenoh-modem's routers run
catalog  = "ab76ec37"               # catalog.json, which the ground holds

[transport]
lease_ms             = 240000
keep_alive           = 4            # a keep-alive every 60 s, which a frame a minute replaces
wait_before_close_ms = 240000       # at least the lease
sequence             = "16bit"
batch_bytes          = 222          # the radio's 220 B SDU and 2 B of stream framing
open_timeout_ms      = 10000
accept_timeout_ms    = 10000
interests_timeout_ms = 10000

[face.rf]
far              = "ground"
attach           = "client"
select           = { link_protocols = ["unixsock-stream"] }
class            = "constrained"
expose           = "link"
interval_s       = 60
max_outage_s     = 3600
link_bps         = 2400
loss_ppm         = 50000            # 5 %
arq              = false            # no link ARQ on the radio (zenoh-modem's tracker)
reply_timeout_ms = 15000            # 16 full batches take 11.8 s
horizon_s        = 120              # one frame a minute affords a 120 s horizon

[face.rf.frames]
"modem.v3/frames/link"   = { every_s = 60 }
"modem.v3/frames/sdu"    = { every_s = 60 }
"modem.v3/frames/sched"  = { every_s = 60 }
"modem.v3/frames/air"    = { every_s = 60 }
"modem.v3/frames/layer"  = { every_s = 60 }
"modem.v3/frames/if"     = { every_s = 60 }
"modem.v3/frames/radio"  = { every_s = 60 }
"modem.v3/frames/bearer" = { every_s = 60 }

description: link.v2's plan (v2.md §2.3, §2.4, §2.7, §2.8, §2.12, §2.16, §2.17, §2.18). Each case is a face policy, `policy`, and a deployment as link.v1's plan.json writes it (`implements`, `contracts` loaded from the repository's root, or `interfaces` inline). `expect` is `{refused}`, the findings that refuse it (a policy's linter's, warnings included, or a deployment's errors alone, link.v1 §2.3), or the plan: `binding`, `catalog` (null when the policy names none), `transport` (null for a link.v1 policy) and `faces`, each face as link.v1's plan.json writes it with `reply_timeout_ms` for a link.v2 face. A face's plan carries `frames` for a link.v2 face with `frames`: each listed frame that crosses, `{resource, every_s, keyframe_s}`, and none for an empty `frames` (§2.3). A case's own `catalog`, where it gives one, is the core §8.6 catalog the far side holds (§2.18); an inline revision has no fingerprint, so a case about the catalog loads contracts. An inline resource may state `type`, its type's kind: `packed` is packed, and any other or none is not (§2.17). `narrow` names principals: `expect.narrowed` gives, for each, the link protocols a subject bound to it is selected by (link.v1 §2.4 over the binding's list), null when no face excludes any. A device face (§2.5) names its devices by address: `implements` maps a listed service's name, or a device's `<system>/<service>`, to its interfaces, and its plan's `attach` is `{shape: "device", devices}`. An inline interface may state `uses`, which a device's `presence_required` reads for `redundancy.v1`, and an inline resource `epoch`, the parameter its template declares as its epoch (`epoch_on_device`). The device cases, from case 22, were written by reading the text, not derived by the reference.
